utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: -- which is "Reserve." And "DDO"?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MAJSTOROVIC
utterances.text: That is the active military personnel.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: And the marking "RVI"?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MAJSTOROVIC
utterances.text: That means the wartime disabled or invalids.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: And the marking "N"?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MAJSTOROVIC
utterances.text: "N" is "missing in action."

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: And "Z"?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MAJSTOROVIC
utterances.text: "Z" stands for "taken prisoner."

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: And "MUP"?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MAJSTOROVIC
utterances.text: Those were members of the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Does the marking "PS" also appear in these instructions?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MAJSTOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: To whom did that marking refer?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MAJSTOROVIC
utterances.text: It was the members of the guard and the members who were there under contract; in other words, they were members of the department, officials.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: So the professional members had a reference of that kind?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MAJSTOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: In this list, the time of engagement, the date of 8 April, '92, is most referred to.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MAJSTOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: What was established on that day and what happened that day so that this date figures most frequently in this list?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MAJSTOROVIC
utterances.text: Officially, on 8 April 1992, it was considered to be the HVO day, but on that day, a state of war was declared in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Did you say the HVO day or the day of the establishment of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MAJSTOROVIC
utterances.text: The day of the establishment of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Regarding the time which is also mentioned in that rubric, next to the marking 2, two dates appear very frequently, one in '94 and one in '96. Could you say whether there were some events referring to those two dates when demobilisation of the reserves took place?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MAJSTOROVIC
utterances.text: You mean the demobilisation of the reserves in '94?

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MAJSTOROVIC
utterances.text: In early 1994, the Washington Agreement was signed, but as part of the implementation of this agreement, the HVO had to reduce its numbers, and therefore demobilisation of part of the HVO forces took place. They kept their wartime assignments but they turned in their weapons and their equipment.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: How did it happen that the persons who claimed that they were demobilised in 1994 still received certain certificates claiming that they were demobilised in 1996? Did you receive any explanation for that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MAJSTOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. This was a temporary demobilisation, and all conscripts retained their wartime assignment because the war in Bosnia and Herzegovina had not yet finished. So that later on, all these military conscripts were still called up to go to the front lines.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Some or all?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MAJSTOROVIC
utterances.text: Some, depending on the needs of particular units.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: What then happened in 1996? Did a final demobilisation take place based on those agreements?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MAJSTOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. In early 1996, the Dayton Accords were implemented, and the final demobilisation -- demobilisation of -- the 92nd Home Guard unit was demobilised and the final demobilisation was completed by 22 April 1996.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: So the final demobilisation in the area which we're focused on, the Vitez municipality, was carried out in April 1996 as part of the implementation of the Dayton Accords; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MAJSTOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Not only in the territory of Vitez municipality but throughout Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Can you also tell me, what did you do based on the list which was given to you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MAJSTOROVIC
utterances.text: On the basis of the lists provided to us at the Department of Defence, we officially received them, we verified them, that is, the accuracy of all the information, that is, the basic information, that is, first and last name, the registration number, the numbers from the registration books, the military registration books, and we had to also enter all the data regarding the calculation of the soldiers' salaries.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Did your duties also include the control of the information which was provided to you in these lists?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MAJSTOROVIC
utterances.text: No. Regarding the information provided us in these lists, we did not have to verify the accuracy of that information. Those who had signed off on these duties had such duty.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: So you said that in addition to the lists which we saw, this was a list of the members of Vitez Brigade and its reserves --

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MAJSTOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: -- that, at the same time, another list was compiled which bears the heading of the HDZ. I would like the usher to please give the witness the document which is P371. Mr. Majstorovic, are you familiar with this list? Have you seen it before?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MAJSTOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: When was this list compiled, drafted?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MAJSTOROVIC
utterances.text: At the same time as the other lists, only referring to the 92nd detachment.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: So what year was that?

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Will you please now look at the first page of the list itself?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MAJSTOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: The heading of this list is "Participants of the Organised Resistance to the Aggression." Can you tell us, knowing what you know, what type of list was this?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MAJSTOROVIC
utterances.text: In instructions received in 1996 for additional pay to soldiers, the instructions say that the additional pay could be calculated as of 18 September 1991.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Why was that day picked? Why was it relevant?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MAJSTOROVIC
utterances.text: That was the date of the initial aggression against Bosnia and Herzegovina which was the attack on Ravno in the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina which bordered on Croatia but it is located in Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Who was to compile that list and who was included in that list?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MAJSTOROVIC
utterances.text: Since, in 1996, we needed to compile this list and the instructions were that the municipal council was --

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: You mean Vitez?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MAJSTOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, the municipal council of Vitez was put in charge of that, and that on the ground, the demobilisation of the civilian protection, that is, the members of the civilian protection in the areas around Vitez was already carried out. The only body which was able to carry out the compilation of this list in the villages and in the town itself were the HDZ structures. So the list which I have in front of me contains all participants of the resistance against the aggression since 1991 who, at that time, had initially self-organised and had so-called village guards with the purpose of protecting life and property in the areas where they were living.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: On the basis of what law did they have the right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MAJSTOROVIC
utterances.text: Anybody who was involved in the period between 19 September 1991 and 22 April 1996 was eligible, and the people who stayed in their villages and did guard duties there were made eligible for this right.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: In the instructions which you said served as a basis for compilation of this list, would it mean that all other participants who in any other way participated in defensive duties were also eligible for such additional pay?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MAJSTOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: So the village guards would fall within that category?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MAJSTOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, as well as all other participants of the war who, in any other way, made it possible for life to go on in a normal way.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: These lists were signed by three persons. Will you please look, let's say, at the bottom of that page which is in front of you. Is the president of the basic branches listed?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MAJSTOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: And the commander?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MAJSTOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Who was the commander?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MAJSTOROVIC
utterances.text: The commander at the time when the lists were compiled, in this case in 1996.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: And the coordinator?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MAJSTOROVIC
utterances.text: The coordinator was the person who assisted in compiling; in other words, it would be the note-taker or scribe.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: So the persons listed here are the persons who were involved in compiling this document in 1996 and their duties refer to the duties which they were carrying out at the time of the compilation of these lists?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MAJSTOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Could you then tell me whether there were any additional persons involved in compiling these documents?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MAJSTOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Who was it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MAJSTOROVIC
utterances.text: Since this list was compiled on the basis of instructions and the municipal leadership was put in charge, it was the president of the municipality who gave his agreement. That would be the local mayor at the relevant time frame.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: And this list was compiled according to territorial principle by a local Communist; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MAJSTOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Tell me, are there HDZ members who are on this list?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MAJSTOROVIC
utterances.text: All persons who were living in these parts who were engaged in defence duties are listed here. Not all of them are members of the HDZ. It is impossible for everyone in a village, for example, to be members of a single party.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: So on this list are military conscripts from a certain place; could we put it that way?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MAJSTOROVIC
utterances.text: No, not only military conscripts, also persons who were incapable of military duty because they gave a contribution as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: And who were involved in certain tasks; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MAJSTOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, in village guards.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Tell us, please, why was this list compiled separately from that of the Vitez Brigade that I showed you a few minutes ago?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MAJSTOROVIC
utterances.text: For a simple reason, because officially not a single military conscript can have a certificate stating that he was a member of a military formation before the 8th of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MAJSTOROVIC
utterances.text: Officially, that date was when the state of war and immediate threat of war was declared.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Before the 8th of April, was there a military formation at all?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MAJSTOROVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: On the 8th of April, was a military formation formed or was this only the beginning of the inception of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MAJSTOROVIC
utterances.text: This was only the inception of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Please tell us, on the basis of this list and the list of the Vitez Brigade, were certain resources distributed and were these lists final?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MAJSTOROVIC
utterances.text: No, these lists were not final. They were expanded and corrected later. On the basis of these lists, calculation was made of this additional pay. In 1997, the list was expanded and certificates were issued for additional pay for members of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Why was the list expanded and how was this done?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MAJSTOROVIC
utterances.text: At the end of 1997, it was realised that our Federal partner had given quite a significant amount for their additional salaries, so in the coming stage of privatisation, the Croatian segment would not have enough to buy shares in companies and in terms of real estate as well, so that's why the list was expanded.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: How was the list expanded?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MAJSTOROVIC
utterances.text: On the basis of a document that we received. The list could have been expanded so as to include all members of the Civil Defence and persons who had work duty, who responded to call-up, or who contributed to ensuring the functioning of the living situation of the population during the war. Therefore, we expanded this list with military conscripts who were elderly and who helped in a way or, rather, participated in defence tasks, together with participants who were women who, in a way through the Civil Defence, helped the military. On the basis all of this that I have mentioned, a certain amount of money was obtained. It was about 3 billion Deutschmark. On that basis, certificates on additional pay for the RBH were issued.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Was this a final list then?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MAJSTOROVIC
utterances.text: This money was never actually given out. This list was not a final one, because the International Community had set the amount is for additional salaries in Bosnia-Herzegovina, up to about 15 billion marks. So the federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina were allocated seven and a half billion, approximately. Mr. Westendorp, as the international arbiter, gave the military component of the HVO about a billion and a half marks. Because of this amount of a billion and a half, there had to be a drastic reduction of the additional salaries that had been calculated.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Then after that decision yet a third list was made; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MAJSTOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: There were certain reductions; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MAJSTOROVIC
utterances.text: In which respect?

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: In respect of deductions.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MAJSTOROVIC
utterances.text: In 1998, certificates were given out with the initial calculations. In the beginning of 1999, there were these drastic cuts. All persons above the -- above a certain age, that is to say, all those who were older than persons born in 1930 or younger than those born in 1978 were deprived of this right. And 1.600 marks were given out. All members of the Civil Defence received 1.200 marks, and all families of persons killed in the war for the homeland received 1.200 marks.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, according to this third list, were these additional salaries paid out?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MAJSTOROVIC
utterances.text: On the basis of these decisions, the Ministry of Defence sent to Sarajevo, to the federal Ministry, to the accounting office, they sent these lists. This past month was a month for corrections and also for lodging complaints, because people were not satisfied and they lodged complaints in terms of the amounts concerned. Therefore, these accounts have not been made final yet.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: These two documents that you see in front of you, that we showed to you, that is P353 and P371, those are the first versions of the list; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MAJSTOROVIC
utterances.text: No. This is only a working material.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: A working material for what?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MAJSTOROVIC
utterances.text: A working material for accounts.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: But these are not the final versions, right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MAJSTOROVIC
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: These two lists were taken from your office; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MAJSTOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. On the 23rd of September, 1998.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Can you just say who took these documents out?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MAJSTOROVIC
utterances.text: The investigators of The Hague Tribunal. They came with a warrant issued by the Court, on the morning of the 23rd of September, 1998. They were accompanied by SFOR.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Was something else taken away except for this paper?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MAJSTOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. A lot of other lists were also taken away. Most of these things were working materials that were used for calculating the shares concerned, and hard disks were taken out of computers and quite a few documents. I don't know exactly what these documents are.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Did you get a list of documents that were taken away by the investigators of the Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MAJSTOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, we did. Not within the deadline provided in the warrant, but we did.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: One more question. The members of SFOR, were they armed as they entered your premises?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MAJSTOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they were. Yes. They had long rifles.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Majstorovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Mr. President, we have some documents here, that is to say, the law and the instructions for elaborating these documents that the witness brought along. However, we did not manage to have them translated. Would it be necessary for these documents to be recognised by the witness and then perhaps tomorrow or the day after tomorrow we could have these documents tendered, if the Prosecutor agrees, and if you agree to that. We can read certain parts of these documents that we have been invoking.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: We could, yes. Maybe tomorrow you could, yes, provide us with the original and the translation tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Mr. Blaxill?

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: I presume there are no other questions from other Defence counsel, Your Honour, so thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Mr. Majstorovic, good morning, to you, sir. My name is Michael Blaxill.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MAJSTOROVIC
utterances.text: Morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: I am one of the prosecuting counsel in this case so I do have a few questions that I'd like to ask you as a result of what you've said here today. Now, if I can just be sure that I understand the two lists that you have referred to, I believe you have said that this list, which we've marked P353, is, in fact, essentially a list from the Viteska Brigade or was the Viteska Brigade; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MAJSTOROVIC
utterances.text: This is a list of the brigade that was during the war called the Vitez Brigade, the Viteska Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: That is the brigade that subsequently became the 92nd Home Guard Regiment; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MAJSTOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: This list was compiled, I believe, if I heard you correctly, by the brigade staff themselves; is that right? They provided this information; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MAJSTOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: So was the information actually provided on the sheets in this format so that you just put it together in your office, or did they supply the information and you translated it into your own forms so that it results in that list?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MAJSTOROVIC
utterances.text: No. The list that you have in front of you came from the regiment. They compiled it and we just kept it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: So on that basis, as you had all these sheets of paper added into a list, did you take any steps to verify any or a proportion of signatures that are appearing down the last but one column on each page of the list?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MAJSTOROVIC
utterances.text: No. We did not have the authority to check or verify anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: So as far as you are personally concerned, you did not gather the information for this list, did not compile these pages, and you had no way of verifying the contents, is that right, yourself personally?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MAJSTOROVIC
utterances.text: Persons from the defence department simply put this together physically. We did not -- this document that you have in front of you, we could not verify it. We could not take part in the elaboration of this list. I personally am on that list so I had to go and sign it, that's all.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: So beyond that, if I asked you about any matter of accuracy in that list, any fact represented there like a name or a signature, except for your own, you clearly -- that would not be within your personal knowledge; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MAJSTOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Thank you. If I can turn, sir, to the other list. We've numbered this P371. You say that that list was prepared by the -- let's say the party administration of the HDZ. Would that be correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MAJSTOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. One of the protagonists of this activity was chairman of the basic organisation of the HDZ, and they were the only structure that could carry this out at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: So is it again true to say, sir, that as regards your own personal experience, your own personal work, you had no part in the preparation of the contents of this list; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MAJSTOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Not a single official from the defence department could take part in any way in the elaboration of this list.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Now, forgive me, sir, because I don't speak or understand your language, but I believe at the top of the pages, in this particular list we've marked 371, underneath the large word in heavy type, can you just tell me what that means? It looks like "Orgahizirani Otpor Agresiji." Could you give me a translation of that? I see my friend smiling, so I've said it very badly. Could you give me a translation?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MAJSTOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. You translated it well. These are participants in organised resistance to the aggression, and in this way they only legalised their very own initiative of gathering together and protecting their lives and property, because in this period in 1991, the former Yugoslav People's Army carried out movements of its own manpower throughout Bosnia-Herzegovina, and they armed their own population, the Serb population, throughout Bosnia-Herzegovina. They gave them weapons. Automatically the number of lootings and robberies went up, and all of this created a lack of security and safety among the population of Vitez. Therefore, these people, at their own initiative, rallied together, organised themselves, organised night patrols or village guards in that context.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Just looking at these two lists side by side, it would appear that the HDZ list ends with the date of the 8th of April, 1992 and the Viteska Brigade begins with the date of the 8th of April, 1992. Would you agree with that, sir, on the face of those documents?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MAJSTOROVIC
utterances.text: It does not necessarily mean that the participants in organised resistance were only from the 8th of April, 1992. Also, this could have related to May 1992. However, this original list had to be compiled by the 8th of April because it has special status. Officially, from the 8th of April, 1992, there could have been a military formation on the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina. The period before that was only a question of persons who were part of the local population, because you can see that this is all done according to places of residence. In other words, villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: But what I'm suggesting, sir, is that HDZ list essentially covers all those persons who formed part of the defensive efforts, or gathering together for defensive purposes, prior to formation of the HVO, and it seems that other lists were then prepared after the formation of the HVO. Would that be fair to say?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MAJSTOROVIC
utterances.text: On the first list, as I mentioned, not all persons of members of the HDZ, and it is -- it carries the heading "HDZ," not because they were all members of the HDZ, but that was the only structure that to compile this list in '96, because in '91 there were still lots of communists in these places where they live. But that was the way in which persons were engaged in such activities, with a view to carrying out organised resistance against aggression, and they are on these lists and, therefore, one cannot say these are a list of members of the HDZ. This was only compiled by persons who at that time were chairmen of basic organisations of the HDZ.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: I accept, sir, you saying that the HDZ were simply the mechanism to prepare this list and this embraces a lot more people. Would it be true to say though that the people in the HDZ list, and I'm not suggesting they're members of it, are all Croat names? Would that be true in that list, to the best of your recollection?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MAJSTOROVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. In 1991 and 1992, I did not live in the territory of Vitez municipality, and I actually am a refugee from Zenica, so I cannot confirm that all the people listed here are actually Croats.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, moving forward from those lists, it seems that you say that you took up duty in 1994 in the defence department, firstly dealing with structures outside the armed forces; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MAJSTOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: What kind of structures were those that you had responsibility for?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MAJSTOROVIC
utterances.text: The official who works on lists of people outside of the armed forces would be involved, those who were on work duty, working in civil protection, then worked on compiling an inventory of the available motor vehicles and livestock.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Now, I know you took up that post in 1994, but would, at that time, the medical services have come under that kind of non-armed forces structure, for instance, volunteer ambulance drivers or people dealing with medical services and supply for the HVO?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MAJSTOROVIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure I understood exactly in what context you put this medical services.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Well, I am suggesting, sir, that anybody who would set up, for instance, first aid supplies, the provision of ambulance or ambulance driving, duties of that nature, obtaining medical supplies themselves, would that have counted as an armed forces activity or would that have been an activity in one of these structures outside the armed forces?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MAJSTOROVIC
utterances.text: Military formations had their own medical service, so if a soldier were mobilised during the war and was within a unit and carrying out such duties, he would be part of the military structure, but if he were in a health centre, in a hospital, then he would have been on work duty.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, do you have any knowledge of what the mobilisation position was, what the difficulties were of mobilisation, back in, let's say, the middle of or late 1992 or early 1993? Did you have any contact with that world?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MAJSTOROVIC
utterances.text: No, I did not. I did not live in Vitez at the time. I only arrived there in the middle of 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: And, in fact, prior to the middle of 1993, is it correct you were, in fact, yourself a soldier; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MAJSTOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I was a member of the reserve forces of the Zenica HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Were you a squad commander in that role?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MAJSTOROVIC
utterances.text: I was a squad commander of a reserve, but I was never deployed anywhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: I see. The unit you belonged to, was that, in fact, the Zenica Brigade? As a reservist.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MAJSTOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. The so-called Jure Francetic Zenica Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Yes, I was going to ask you that, sir, as a matter of curiosity. That was the Jure Francetic Brigade. Thank you. So your first contact, you say now, was, in fact, in 1994 and that you remained engaged in work regarding the system of these additional salaries until what date? Are you still involved in that kind of work?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MAJSTOROVIC
utterances.text: I have been working in that duty since 1996 and I am still involved in this duty.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: All right. Now, just to go back to one date, that is the very first date referred to in these lists, in fact, it was the 8th of -- sorry, the 18th of September, 1991. You take that as a kind of outbreak-of-hostilities date. Was that, in fact, when conflict developed between Croatia and the Serbs and that the attack on Rovna was simply because that was just over the border in Bosnia-Herzegovina; do I understand that correctly?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MAJSTOROVIC
utterances.text: The conflict between the Serbs and the Croats broke out in April 1991, so it's not directly related to that conflict, but this was an incursion of the former JNA into the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Thank you for clarifying that, sir. Sir, just to recap one very brief point. The reality is that as regards these lists that are in the court today, you personally have no way of assisting as to the accuracy of their contents? I know I'm repeating myself, but just to confirm that one point. Is that right, sir?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MAJSTOROVIC
utterances.text: Officials of the defence department could, only in cases where there were some egregious mistakes, to enter any corrections on the spot if they really found them but in no other ways were permitted to make any additional corrections. There were instances when some members, let's say by a mistake of an official who was entering the data or when it was typed, somebody entered the first half of 1991, but no participant of the war for homeland could have had such date admitted. Only as of 18 September. So only such egregious mistakes could be corrected and no other ones.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Your Honour, that concludes my cross-examination. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Counsel Slokovic-Glumac?

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Mr. Majstorovic, you said that you were a squad commander; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MAJSTOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Were you a soldier or reservist?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MAJSTOROVIC
utterances.text: Reservist.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: So that was your wartime assignment?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MAJSTOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: So at that time you were not militarily involved?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MAJSTOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. That is what I have said.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: So when were you militarily involved?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MAJSTOROVIC
utterances.text: Only upon my arrival in the Vitez municipality.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: This is the time when you became a soldier?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MAJSTOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that was the time when I became a soldier.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: The Prosecutor asked you, in reference to these two lists, that he believed that the first list ends -- that the second list starts where the first one ends?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MAJSTOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. And that is normal.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Were the participants of the village guards included in the second list as well?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MAJSTOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. And this is why these two lists are linked.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: What is the title, what is the categorisation which a member of the village guard got in the second -- based on the instructions you received?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MAJSTOROVIC
utterances.text: It would be the status "P" or "Reserves."

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: So the difference between the two listings is really just by the methods; they refer to different periods but it refers to the same persons?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MAJSTOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: These persons had a status of the reserves until when?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MAJSTOROVIC
utterances.text: Up until the date of the mobilisation.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: I apologise. When did they receive the status of reserves?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MAJSTOROVIC
utterances.text: They all were reserves.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: And when did they receive the status of soldier?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MAJSTOROVIC
utterances.text: First it is entered when he is recruited, then he is taken to training, and then he becomes a soldier.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: So not at the time of the mobilisation?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MAJSTOROVIC
utterances.text: Those who are mobilised have a status of a soldier in reserve.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Let me take you back to it from the beginning. How do people get recruited?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MAJSTOROVIC
utterances.text: A recruit is entered in the list of military recruits when he reaches the age of 17.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: And at that time, is he a soldier?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MAJSTOROVIC
utterances.text: At that time, he is a recruit. He is then sent for a medical examination and he gets an evaluation, whether he is fit or unfit for military service. Then he receives a VES.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: What is a VES?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MAJSTOROVIC
utterances.text: That is the military specialisation. Every branch of the armed forces has their own specialisations, and on the basis of that, he is then called up for military duty. When he is fully 18 years old, he can be called up.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: During the period when he is performing his military service, is he a soldier?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MAJSTOROVIC
utterances.text: He is a soldier.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: After he is finished with his military service and he becomes a member of the reserves, is he still a soldier?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MAJSTOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. He is a soldier who has no particular assignment and awaits his military assignment.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: So according to you, everybody is a member of the reserves?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MAJSTOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. They are all soldiers in reserve.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: So when a mobilisation takes place of the military reserves, what happens then?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MAJSTOROVIC
utterances.text: Everybody is called up. So all military recruits, reservists who have no assignments, are then called up by the unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: After the demobilisation, he again is transferred back to the reserves; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MAJSTOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Do you know when demobilisation of the military reserve forces in the Vitez municipality was conducted in April 1994? Do you have that information?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MAJSTOROVIC
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: When was the reserve force mobilised in the territory of the Vitez municipality in April 1993? Can you pinpoint the date?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MAJSTOROVIC
utterances.text: No, I cannot. I was not a resident in the Vitez municipality at that time.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Very well. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you, Counsel Slokovic-Glumac. We don't have any questions for the witness. Mr. Majstorovic, thank you for testifying. You may now be released. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Counsel Slokovic-Glumac, are you going to call any of the accused or any other witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Mr. President, before calling the first and the second accused, we have certain problems to report. The Prosecution is aware of the fact and the Trial Chamber may be aware of the fact that we have requested that certain documents be entered into evidence. Allow me just to look up the appropriate dates. The documents referring to the Vitez Brigade, these are D36/2, D37/2, and D38/2, also the document D16/2, I would like to request my colleagues from the Prosecution, since they know what these documents are, to just say whether they accept these documents, especially given the fact that they were admitted in Blaskic and they were admitted there without any objection on the part of the Prosecution team in that case.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I just need a few minutes to see what kind of documents we are talking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Are you speaking of some orders signed by General Blaskic?

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: That is correct. Mr. President, the following is at issue: The proceedings in the Blaskic case are completed, and documents were admitted there which were confirmed by two witnesses without any objections. It was confirmed by both General Blaskic and by Slavko Marin. And the fourth document, in addition to the orders of General Blaskic, the fourth document was also admitted without any objections. What is my point? I believe that the Prosecution needs to have a consistent position with respect to the documents which are being submitted in different cases. I believe that the Prosecution would probably like to cross-examine on these documents, but if they admit these documents without any objections and, in our case, they object to their admission and deny their authenticity, I believe that it is unethical to take different positions in different cases regarding the same facts. The Prosecution is one and a single body. They work together and they should have the same position with respect to facts. So if they decide to admit to something in one case and not in another, we will find ourselves in a situation where we will end up with different results based on the same facts. I would just like to know what the position of the Prosecution is with respect to these documents at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Before I give the floor to the Prosecution, let me remind you that, to the best of my recollection, we already decided on those documents, and I think they are signed by General Blaskic, and I vividly remember that I asked you to call General Blaskic to say in court whether or not he recognises his signature, and there was no follow-up to my suggestion, so therefore, those documents were not admitted into evidence. As for the position of the Prosecution, it is, of course, for the Prosecution to tell us whether or not they take the same stand here as in another trial.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Mr. President, I was just going to further clarify this. I would just like to know what the position of the Prosecution is at this time. We talked to General Blaskic's Defence team regarding the question which you raised and we were told that he is not going to testify here because he is preparing his defence and he is involved in his case. We also contacted Slavko Marin, who had testified in the Blaskic case, and we thought that he would come here, he was actually announced last week to come and testify, because we wanted to verify certain documents and introduce certain documents through him and also verify their authenticity. Only today we learned that he is not coming at all. Thirdly, during the last break between the two sessions, my colleague Radovic and I were in Vitez, and we searched for other people who would be able to verify the authenticity of these documents. Among the people who were at the Operative Zone headquarters at the time, very few of them were there, and Franjo Nakic, who was present, refused to come and testify based on medical grounds. So our position is that it is very difficult for us to locate a witness. We believe that the documents are very important for us, for our defence, and Mr. Radovic and I are unable to complete our case until these documents are admitted; and also, if the position of the Prosecution does not change and if the Trial Chamber does not rule based on Rule 94(B), we would be forced to interrupt our case until such time as we are able to locate a witness who will be able to authenticate our case, our documents, because we find them absolutely relevant for our defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: You will not be interrupting the case, Mrs. Slokovic-Glumac. You will be applying to the Trial Chamber to interrupt the case. That's the first thing.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The second thing is this: The more important the document, the more important it is made authentic, that it is authenticated by a witness. The third is that it is a matter for the Trial Chamber to rule on the evidence in this case, not on the evidence in other case, as to whether we should admit the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Mr. Terrier?

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. When these documents were presented to the Court on the 13th of January, 1999, we noticed that there were certain grounds for suspicion, because some documents did not have numbers of orders, something had been deleted, and then Zvonimir Cilic, the witness who then testified, was not in a position to identify them. That is why we did not want these documents to be entered into evidence, and we think that the Trial Chamber ruled as it ruled. I would have a proposal, in view of the fact that I cannot change my opinion today because we have not received a single new element in this respect. These documents are yet to be proven authentic. I listened to Mr. Pavkovic very attentively, and he said that he would give up on calling Slavko Marin as a witness. We did not want to extend this discussion, because we thought that alibi was up. I thought that Mr. Pavkovic did not know why Mr. Marin decided on his own initiative to not to come a witness before this Court and not to respond to the Defence's invitation for him to testify. So I wonder, should we not look into everything? That is to say, the Prosecution and the Defence, shouldn't we all look into this together? Isn't it mandatory for Slavko Marin to come and testify? Is it not up to the Defence to establish the alibi of Vlado Santic but also reveal the truth before this Trial Chamber? I believe that Slavko Marin, in view of his position during these events, can give some information that would be indeed valuable to the Court in their quest for the truth. Also, he could provide information which would identify the documents that are under discussion today. It is for that reason that I request from the Trial Chamber today, in view of the information that we received from Mr. Pavkovic and in view of the concerns expressed by Mrs. Slokovic-Glumac, to consider whether it would be a good thing to call Mr. Pavkovic (sic) as a Court witness perhaps when we sit again, perhaps in the month of August or whenever. It was probably a slip of the tongue. I think it's pretty obvious that it was a slip of the tongue. I also wish to add and thus conclude that this is a measure that the Court had already taken in the case of a witness that was supposed to be called by the Prosecution and for whom the Prosecutor decided that it was not necessary to call him. So it would not be the first time that the Court reached such a decision, but I think that it is truly justified now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: May I ask Counsel Pavkovic to comment on this suggestion by the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, I don't really know what I could say that would be new by way of a comment. Mr. Slavko Marin was on our list as a witness on the list of the Defence for Vladimir Santic, and he was on that list for the 8th of July of this year. Already on the 9th I explained to the Court that I did not know the real reasons for the fact that he did not come. When I looked into the matter and when I talked to my client about the situation concerning documents, because two other witnesses had testified. Davor Biletic and testified and Ivica Franic had testified in the meantime. It was our assessment that irrespective of the reasons why Slavko Marin did not come, that we would give up on his testimony. I wanted to say that yesterday, but I did not want to interrupt witness Bringa. I don't see what more I could add to this. You're quite right, Mr. President. You gave me the right to decide on this witness, so that was my assessment and I didn't want to burden you with this any longer. We had simply decided not to call him as a witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Counsel Slokovic-Glumac, could you please tell me about D36/2? Is it a document, an order signed by General Blaskic? So these are three orders signed by --

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: That's right. That's right. These are three orders.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: And D16/2 is signed by Mr. Ljubicic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Pasko Ljubicic, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Our ruling it as follows: We don't intend to call as a Court witness Mr. Slavko Marin because we feel that this would not be fair to the accused. We do intend to call General Blaskic, only for the purpose of authenticating the three orders in D36/2, 37, 38. So we will issue an order to call him as a Court witness for this exclusive purpose. That's our ruling. Yes, Counsel Slokovic-Glumac?

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: I don't know whether this is a mistake in the transcript, but General Blaskic, during his testimony, did recognise document D16/2. This is a report of the military police, because this report was sent to him and he had received it on that day, that is to say, the 16th in the afternoon. At any rate, he can confirm that this document was received by him on that day and that ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: May I just add one more thing in relation to these documents and our attitude towards them? Mr. President, we would like, at any rate, that Mr. Blaskic make a statement concerning the authenticity of these documents before Zoran and Mirjan Kupreskic present their defence. We would like, in our part of the case, that their testimonies be the last thing that we do and that we conclude our case with their own defences. So would it be possible to organise it that way? You said yourself the statement he would be making would be extremely brief and he would simply be confirm their authenticity. So could it please precede their statements?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes. Sorry, yes?

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Counsel Radovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, we have another problem. We asked the Trial Chamber to give us leave to lodge an appeal with regard to the documents the Prosecutor can present when a witness is testifying, so we agree with the witnesses who testify in Court. These statements can be presented. They are admitted as evidence. Then also statements of witnesses who were not in Court but who were not submitted to the Defence counsel in any form, they cannot be tendered. We agree with that too. However, we do not agree with the possibility to present statements of witnesses who were not heard in Court and that the Prosecutor has, and they were obtained in some way. For example, statements that were given before an investigative Judge in Zenica or wherever. We would appreciate it if when our clients are heard as witnesses, we know exactly and finally what is legally binding and what can they be shown during their testimony on a valid basis. So please, could our clients not be heard as witnesses in this case until we definitely know the rules under which they will be heard? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: But you see, it will take some time. First of all, your appeal will go to a panel of three Judges, members of the Appeals Chamber. Then they have to decide whether or not to grant leave to appeal. Then there will be an appeal. There will be, of course, briefs filed by yourself and the Prosecution. So probably it will take one or two months for the Appeals Chamber to decide on this matter. So I don't see why we should stop now and reconvene in September or October only because this issue has not been settled by the Appeals Chamber. You can, of course, stress in your appeal the urgency of the matter, but it is for the President of the Appeals Chamber to decide also on when to decide on this matter. So it's beyond our control. As a Trial Chamber, we have no say. Of course we must not interfere in any way with the Appeals Chamber. We can't. So as I say, I don't see why we should wait until the decision of the Appeals Chamber to call and hear the two accused you mentioned before. We can't do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes, Counsel Radovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, when Mr. Terrier, as a representative of the Prosecution, argued why he is asking for testimonies of persons who had not testified here, it was precisely to introduce witnesses whom you had not heard, that you would be given an opportunity to make sure that they are witnesses of truth. This is our concern too, because we would have to match their testimony against the testimony of somebody that you never heard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: All right. Now, we have two issues. The first issue, General Blaskic. We will now call General Blaskic, and we very much hope that he will be able to give evidence tomorrow morning at 9.00. I will issue an order accordingly, as soon as this hearing is over. However, if he can't come tomorrow -- I know that there is no hearing this week in the Blaskic case, so he should be available tomorrow morning. If for any reason he can't come tomorrow at 9.00 or maybe on Thursday and so on, we will proceed in any case with the accused, because I don't see any point in waiting for General Blaskic if only because we have to see what he's going too say about those three documents. But as I say, of course, the order to be issued will specify that the he should come here and give evidence on those particular points tomorrow at 9.00, but if for any particular reason he can't, we will go on with the witnesses to be called by Defence counsel. As for the other issue, let me ask Mr. Terrier of the Prosecution whether they intend to use, in cross-examination, those documents to which the Defence is objecting and which has filed an appeal before the Appeals Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's a little bit difficult to say right now which documents we're going to use for the cross-examination. We could consider using a certain number of statements that were given by witnesses under circumstances and conditions that were indicated and specified by the Trial Chamber. I'd like to indicate to Mr. Radovic that in doing so, we are not going to compare a written document or a written statement with an oral statement of someone who was at the Tribunal, but would rather compare the factual situations as appear in the written statements in respect of the statements given under oath. This is something completely different from what Mr. Radovic is saying and, once again, I do not have the feeling that in doing so we are putting at risk the rights which the Defence exercises and which the accused exercise. In order to answer your question, Your Honour, today we are unable to eliminate absolutely the possibility of not calling in written testimony which was not disclosed to the Defence previously. Nonetheless, of course, if the Trial Chamber desires, in order to avoid any discussions, we will refrain from acting in that manner and we will do what the Trial Chamber asks us to do. But in light of what was said before this Trial Chamber, in light of the statements that were disclosed to the Defence, we have important material which might be sufficient in order to move forward with the cross-examination appropriately of the accused. In any case, we will comply with the orders of the Trial Chamber. Having said that, Your Honour, I have another question to raise, if this is the proper time, if you will allow me to do so. I understood that both the accused, who will speak first, will be called by the two attorneys; that is, each accused will be the witness of his own case but also a Defence witness for another accused. In this way, for each accused, he will have two examinations in chief but two additional examinations, and I was wondering -- of course, we are facing a situation which is unprecedented here. I was wondering whether this complied with the Rules of Procedure because the accused is not a witness like the other witnesses but is one -- or a person who is authorised to appear as a witness for his own defence according to Rule 98 of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence, and I wonder whether an accused can really appear as a witness for the defence of another person, that is, a person other than himself. In other words, I was wondering whether it is possible and whether it is reasonable to allow each of the accused to be subject to two examinations in chief and then to two cross-examinations and additional examinations. This is a problem which I wanted to raise before Your Honours with full knowledge that perhaps there is material here for stating a procedural position in face of this new situation. I have two other very short comments that I would like to make. At this stage of the trial, we still do not know whether the accused Vladimir Santic plans to appear as a witness in his own defence. Last Friday, Mr. Pavkovic told us that the situation was being reviewed, and my last comment is that Mr. Pavkovic submitted statements -- or affidavits, rather, to the Trial Chamber about the character of the accused on the basis of 94 ter. I would like to ask that the admissibility of these affidavits be postponed and not be admitted as evidence at this point [interpretation error]. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Mr. President, please, with your permission, just in connection with what Mr. Terrier said. Mr. Radovic, a week ago in this Chamber, before this Chamber, said that we would together question the accused when they testify as witnesses, that we would do this in the following way: Certain sections would be handled by one Defence attorney and certain sections would be handled by the other Defence attorney. You have seen from the very outset of this trial that this is a joint defence for Zoran and Mirjan Kupreskic. They have joint witnesses. And when the second accused will be testifying, then perhaps it won't even be necessary to question him on certain points that will already have been taken care of by the first accused. The Prosecutor did not object to that solution on the very first day when we presented it, and we felt that this was all right, and that is how we prepared their defence. We have been preparing this defence for over a week now. Quite a bit of time has gone by. We are supposed to start tomorrow, and now we are supposed to change the methodology, which was not objected to, as I said, at the time when we made that proposal. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: We have decided that when the two accused will be examined, will be called here, there will be no cross-examination by the Prosecution on undisclosed material without leave of the Trial Chamber. So, therefore, whenever you want to raise a matter based on a statement made, signed by a person who has not been called here as a witness, you will have to ask leave from the Trial Chamber to do so, and we will decide case by case. As for the way we go about the examination of the two witnesses, we feel that although our Rules state that an accused may testify on his own behalf, a broad and liberal interpretation should be placed on this Rule; therefore, an accused may also testify on behalf of another accused. I think this is in the interests of the Defence and in the interests of proper administration of justice. In addition, we feel that Counsel Slokovic-Glumac suggested a proper procedure, namely, that each accused will be examined in chief by two counsel, each of them will concentrate on a particular area, and then he will be cross-examined by the other counsel, counsel other than the one who is calling the accused. So there will be examination-in-chief by two counsel, who will divide up the area of concern; and then, as I say, a cross-examination only by one other counsel; and then the Prosecution will proceed to cross-examination. So if, say, Counsel Slokovic-Glumac is calling one of the accused for examination-in-chief, examination-in-chief will be undertaken by both counsel, you and Counsel Radovic; but then the cross-examination will be carried out by Counsel Radovic and vice versa. I hope this is clear. Now, as for the question relating to -- the question of whether or not -- yes, Counsel Slokovic-Glumac?

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Mr. President, my apologies. This is a technical matter, but it may pose a bit of a problem for us. With respect to the cross-examination -- or re-examination, I should say, should be left to our own decision which of the two counsel will conduct it, regardless of who had examined in chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: I would say so, because in any case, we have decided that the examination-in-chief will be carried out by both counsel.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: So it is for you to decide who is going to re-examine the -- yes, I think it is quite proper. Now, moving to this question relating to Mr. Santic, whether or not he will testify. Again, we think that it is for Counsel Pavkovic to decide, not now but at a later stage, because I had a feeling -- I may be wrong -- but I think Counsel Pavkovic gave a hint that he would decide after the examination of the first two accused or maybe the three accused, the three Kupreskics, and I think it is for you to decide at a later stage. We don't want to press you to decide right away.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, what you just said is exactly what Mr. Santic just gave me as a message; in other words, we have been speaking about it for a while, to wait and see, and we will see what the first three accused say. I believe that this will also leave enough time for the Prosecution to also prepare themselves should we decide to call our own client.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes. Let me add a footnote for the Prosecution. I do understand that the Prosecution is put in a rather awkward position because they don't know right away. On the other hand, I think the Prosecution is aware that the Defence counsel come from a country where the civil law system is adopted, and probably in those countries they are not familiar with the examination and cross-examination of the accused. So therefore, I would make allowance for this need by the Defence, to see how it works. All right. So if there is no other outstanding matter, we can adjourn now. As I say, I hope that tomorrow we can start with General Blaskic. If not, we will start with the first of the two accused.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I could ask you for just one moment having to do with the affidavits of Mr. Pavkovic. There was a mistake in the transcript. I am not opposed to their being disclosed, and the opposite had been indicated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: I had forgotten to thank you and to have said that they have been tendered as evidence and admitted. We will now be told the number -- well, perhaps not now. You can do it tomorrow morning. We will adjourn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: 1.00 p.m., to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 14th day of July, 1999, at 9.00 a.m.
